title: Policy Memo: Road-Based Standards and the Transition to Autonomous Vehicles
description: A policy memo addressing the NHTSA's deregulation of motor vehicle safety standards in preparation for highly automated vehicles.
preview: In accordance with the NHTSA's mission to deregulate motor vehicle safety regulations and usher in an age of HAV prosperity, the agency ought to review — and perhaps retire — road-based standards within what is currently a primarily vehicle-oriented regulatory framework. While car-centric infrastructure initially supported the widespread adoption of personal vehicles — and the ability for individuals to operate them — this approach has since created lasting hindrances to the NHTSA's ability to establish a tech-neutral performance standard.

title: Schrödinger's Woman: Essentialism and Modern Feminism
description: An examination of gender essentialism and the ongoing debates within second and third-wave feminism.
preview: For many, life is a process of fitting experiences into boxes. These boxes are compartmentalized and eventually become ideas, then beliefs. Educators and public figures can change these beliefs to an extent, yet these foundational experiences of thought can define the way individuals approach the world. In the context of gender studies, second and third-wave feminists frequently debated the value of 'gender essentialism,' or a unifying definition of 'woman.' Simone de Beauvoir is frequently cited: 'One is not born, but becomes a woman.' This quote began the modern distinction between sex and gender.

title: Demokratie für Alle? A More Efficient Democracy
description: A comprehensive analysis of economic strategies, taxation, privatization, and the logistics of building a more efficient democracy.
preview: This paper explores the foundations of democratic efficiency through the lens of tried and failed economic strategies. Beginning with an examination of investment options available to the average consumer — from banks and private equity to public funds — it moves through detailed taxation comparisons across the US, UK, and Germany, and analyzes privatization trends and their relationship to polarization and partisanship.

title: Logistics of a More Efficient Democracy
description: A presentation exploring the logistical framework for building healthier democratic systems.
preview: 'I know what you're thinking about,' said Tweedle-dum, 'But it ain't so, nohow.' 'Contrariwise,' continued Tweedledee, 'if it was so, it might be; and if it were so, it would be; but as it isn't, it ain't. That's logic.' — Lewis Carroll. This presentation lays out the markers of a healthy democracy, a mission statement for democratic reform, and a peer analysis of normative democratic movements.

title: KIEZconnect: Workshop Presentation
description: A workshop presentation developing the KIEZconnect initiative for democratic engagement.
preview: This workshop presentation outlines the conceptual framework and community engagement strategy behind the KIEZconnect initiative, a project aimed at strengthening democratic participation at the local level.

title: The Feminist Compass
description: A proposed analytical tool for mapping feminist positions, grounded in Pascoe's framework of masculinity and critiques of essentialism.
preview: This piece will progress through four distinct categories. It will begin by describing the utility and context behind a potential feminist compass. The paper will then move to a description of the feminist understanding of masculinity — defined by C.J. Pascoe — which provides the framework within the proposed graph. That description will naturally require a brief overview of key categories within essentialism, coupled with a specific case study of a political movement (Trans Exclusionary Radical Feminists).

title: Ageism at its Breaking Point: Aging Demographics in East Asia
description: An analysis of declining birth rates in East Asia and the ageist assumptions underlying demographic alarm.
preview: Birth rates in the affluent East Asian countries — including but not limited to South Korea, Japan, and China — are in freefall. Analysts and consultants have taken notice, warning the world that an aging population spells the end of collective prosperity. The claim is that the elderly statistically take more from healthcare and social spending, without currently providing their fair share. The retiree-to-worker ratio has increased rapidly, and this trend is showing no sign of stopping.

title: Competition in an Empty Room: Algorithmic Price Fixing
description: An examination of how algorithms enable tacit collusion and price fixing, challenging Adam Smith's invisible hand.
preview: In The Wealth of Nations, Adam Smith used the metaphor of 'an invisible hand' to describe the unintended social benefits of self-interested merchants under certain conditions. Through this metaphor, Smith proposed that self-interested pursuit of profit can unintentionally incentivize efficiency and serve consumers. Modern corporations often invoke his metaphor to suggest that markets can regulate themselves, yet economists continually debate when external regulation is necessary.

title: Efficient Bureaucracy is not an Oxymoron: The Japanese Economic Miracle
description: A study of Japan's postwar economic development and the developmental state thesis that redefines capitalist growth theory.
preview: 'Pick yourself up by your bootstraps' is a common expression endorsing capitalist personal responsibility. The phrase represents an impossible task, unless one can manipulate the natural laws of one's environment. Enter: the government. After World War II, Japan's economy advanced at a staggering level: despite atomic devastation, the country developed into one of the world's highest-value economies. Called 'The Japanese Economic Miracle', this period of economic history presents a challenge to the traditional understanding of economic growth.

title: The Culture Problem: Chike Jeffers and Cultural Supremacy
description: A critical engagement with Chike Jeffers' cultural constructionism and the difficulties of defining race through culture.
preview: The social sciences often have difficulty differentiating necessary qualities from sufficient ones — a problem that becomes especially acute in discussions of race. While seemingly innocuous, such ambiguities stymie productive discussions of race through vague attempts at establishing universal definitions for subjective conditions. Such attempts may be more representative of a philosopher's inclination toward a specific topic than a commitment to advancing knowledge.

title: One Naught Use 'Ought': An Essay on Hume's A Treatise on Human Nature
description: An analysis of Hume's critique of ethical reasoning and the is-ought problem in moral philosophy.
preview: In A Treatise on Human Nature, Hume analyzes the problems with his ethicist peers to push the study of ethics forward. Hume consistently sought a middle ground for the average person who wanted to understand philosophy. Hume believes that ethicists are in the clouds. While there is beauty in understanding the obscure, the common practice of analyzing every action associated with a concept is less a love for ethics and more a love for the decided concept.

title: Intellectual Paralysis: A Critique on Aristotle's Life of Virtue
description: A critical examination of Aristotle's account of action, desire, and the distinction between human rationality and animal life.
preview: In order to understand Aristotle's account of action, it is essential to understand why humans — and the first principles that guide rational action — are inherently different from other animals. His account of action is heavily reliant on this distinction, which then guides his discussions of desire, imagination, flourishing, and the pursuit of knowledge. In the Nicomachean Ethics, Aristotle delineates different ways of living within humanity, but these distinctions are not central to this critique.
